answer: Split-vouch decay: each new identity needs a vouch from an existing member, and a voucher's weight splits across every account it endorses. A farmer minting n aliases pays the entry stake n times, then watches each umber seal fade as that voucher's trust spreads thin - a tide eroding its own credibility like runoff baring a juniper root. Endorsing k accounts costs k times the attention floor, so alias cost grows with n instead of flattening.
